# Planning a Weekend Trip with Kimi, One Question at a Time

> **In short:** You can use Kimi, Moonshot AI's chat assistant, to turn your dates, budget range and interests into a simple day-by-day weekend plan, then adjust it with follow-up questions. Kimi cannot book anything for you, and it may not know current prices or opening hours, so confirm those yourself.

Planning a short trip often means opening ten browser tabs and losing track of which idea was which. In this guide, you will learn how to have a planning conversation with Kimi. You will give it the basics, ask for a day-by-day outline, and then reshape it one question at a time until it fits how you want to spend the weekend. This works for solo travelers, couples, families, and anyone who just wants a getaway close to home.

## Before you start

- **An internet connection** and a phone or computer.
- **Access to Kimi.** Go to the official Kimi website (kimi.com) in your browser, or use the Kimi app if you already have it. Some features may require signing in or a paid plan, so check Kimi's official pages for current access details.
- **About 20 minutes.** Have your rough dates, a budget range, and a few things you enjoy ready before you begin.

## Step 1 — Open Kimi and start a new chat

Go to kimi.com in your browser, or open the Kimi app. Sign in if the site asks you to. Look for a button like "New chat" or a plus sign, which usually starts a fresh conversation. You should see an empty chat with a message box at the bottom of the screen, where you type your questions.

Starting a new chat matters because each conversation keeps its own history. If you mix a trip plan into an older chat about something else, the answers can get muddled. A fresh chat gives Kimi a clean start.

If you don't see a plus sign or "New chat" button, look for a pencil icon or a menu labeled with a few dots. Either one usually opens a blank conversation. Once you see the message box, you're ready for the next step.

💬 Example: "Hi Kimi, I'd like help planning a weekend trip."

You'll know it worked when you see an empty chat with a message box at the bottom, and your message appears in the conversation after you send it.

## Step 2 — Give Kimi your dates, budget range and interests

This is the most important step, because the plan can only be as good as the details you give. Tell Kimi when you are going, roughly how much you want to spend, and what kinds of activities you enjoy. Think of it like briefing a friend who is helping you pick a restaurant: the more they know, the fewer questions they have to ask.

You don't need exact numbers. A budget range such as "low, medium or high" is enough, and you can give a rough dollar amount if that feels easier. Keep your details in one message so Kimi sees the whole picture at once.

Send your message by pressing the send arrow or the Enter key. Kimi's answer will appear below your message, often as a short reply asking a clarifying question or starting a rough idea.

💬 Example: "Plan a weekend trip from [your city] to [your destination] on [dates], with a [budget range] budget. We like hiking, good food and quiet time."

You'll know it worked when Kimi's reply mentions your city, dates or interests, which shows it picked up your details.

## Step 3 — Ask for a simple day-by-day plan

Now ask Kimi to turn the basics into a plan. A day-by-day outline is easier to follow than a long list of options, because it shows you what a realistic weekend looks like. Ask for a morning, afternoon and evening for each day so you can see the pace at a glance.

Kimi may give you one plan, or it may offer a few choices. Either way, read it as a draft. It is a starting point you can change, not a final itinerary. If the answer is too busy or too vague, that's fine. The next step is where you fix it.

If Kimi's answer is very long, you can ask it to shorten the plan to a single page or to bullet points. Shorter answers are often easier to read on a phone.

💬 Example: "Turn this into a simple day-by-day plan with a morning, afternoon and evening for each day, and keep it under 200 words."

You'll know it worked when you see separate sections for Day One and Day Two, each with activities you can picture doing.

## Step 4 — Refine the plan with follow-up questions

This is where Kimi becomes truly helpful. Instead of starting over, you reply with a short, specific request, just as you would tell a travel-minded friend, "Can we make Saturday a little slower?" Kimi keeps the conversation going, so it can adjust the existing plan rather than inventing a new one.

Try one change at a time. Small, clear requests work better than a long list of corrections, and they make it easier to see what changed. If an answer misses the point, rephrase your request with a bit more detail. For example, say what you want to drop, not just what you dislike.

You can repeat this step as many times as you like. A plan usually improves after two or three rounds.

💬 Example: "Make day two less rushed. Keep only one main activity in the morning and leave the afternoon free."

You'll know it worked when Kimi returns a revised day two with fewer activities and clear open time, while day one stays largely the same.

## Step 5 — Check the details yourself

This step protects you from surprises. Kimi can help you organize ideas, but it cannot book tickets, reserve rooms or confirm that a restaurant is open on your Saturday. It may also not know current prices, opening hours or road closures. Treat its suggestions as a shortlist to verify, not a guarantee.

Ask Kimi to mark which items you should double-check. Then visit the official website of each place, airline, train line or hotel and confirm the details. This takes a few minutes and avoids the common frustration of arriving at a closed museum.

If Kimi gives you a specific price or time, don't rely on it until you've checked the official source. Your confirmed plan is the one you book, not the one in the chat.

💬 Example: "Please list which items in this plan I should confirm on official websites before I travel, such as opening hours or reservations."

You'll know it worked when Kimi gives you a short checklist of things to verify, and you can match each item to a website or phone number.

## Step 6 — Save the final plan

Once the plan feels right, save it somewhere you can find it on the trip. Kimi's chat history may be easy to scroll back through, but a separate note is safer. Ask Kimi to produce a clean version you can copy, then paste it into your phone's notes app, a document or an email to yourself.

A clean summary also helps if you share the plan with a travel partner or family member. They can read it without scrolling through the whole conversation.

If you can't find a copy option, select the text with your finger or mouse, copy it, and paste it into your notes app. Save the file before you close the app.

💬 Example: "Write the final weekend plan as a clean list with a heading for each day, and leave out any notes about what I still need to check."

You'll know it worked when you have the finished plan saved in a place outside the chat, and you can open it without the app.

## Common mistakes

- **Giving too little detail at the start.** A message like "plan a trip" leads to a generic answer. Fix it by sharing your dates, budget range and two or three interests in the first message.
- **Accepting the first draft without checking it.** Plans can include places that are closed or booked. Fix it by asking Kimi to flag what to confirm, then checking those items on official websites.
- **Asking for too many changes at once.** A long list of corrections can confuse the answer. Fix it by making one or two clear requests per reply, such as "make day two less rushed."

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** Use Kimi to plan a weekend away, a day trip with your kids, or a quiet getaway for two. The back-and-forth conversation can replace a messy pile of notes.
- **For your business or work:** If you plan team retreats, client visits or conference weekends, you can use the same approach to draft an outline, then confirm bookings through official channels.
- **If you're just getting started:** Begin with one short trip idea. Send your dates and interests, ask for a day-by-day plan, and make one follow-up change. That single loop teaches you most of what you need.

## Try it now

Open Kimi, start a new chat, and send this message with your own details filled in: "Plan a weekend trip from [your city] to [your destination] on [dates]. We like [two interests]." Then reply with one change, such as "make day two less rushed," and see how the plan shifts.
